name: Oxford Brookes University

settingEvidence.evidence: Headington Campus sits one mile east of Oxford city centre and is made up of three sites:

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students on full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28), as shown on the Brookes course pages; the placement year costs £2,010. The fee was £9,790 in 2026/27. Brookes says Home fees may rise in later years in line with inflation and that it intends to charge the maximum permitted level.

source.evidence: 2027 / 28 Home (UK) full time £10,050

livingCosts.text: Undergraduate halls cost about £139-£255 a week for contracts starting September 2026 (2026/27), from Crescent Hall at £139.02 to the shared Westminster Studios at the Harcourt Hill campus at £255.43; New Clive Booth is from £231.70. Contracts are 38 or 50 weeks. Prices for 2027-28 are expected in January 2027. Brookes' general living-costs guide (no year given) estimates £323-£428 a week in total, or £12,274-£16,264 for a 38-week year.

source.evidence: £139.02 per week

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open days in Oxford: 24 October 2026 and 14 November 2026 (10.00am to 3.30pm, Headington Campus). 2027 dates are not announced yet.

source.evidence: 24 October 2026 - 24 October 2026

contextual.summary: UK applicants who meet one of Brookes' contextual criteria (for example lived in care, refugee status, free school meals, young carer under 25, or completed Brookes Engage), or a school-results plus area combination, can get a contextual offer shown on each course page.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 3 grades below the standard entry requirements

criteria.detail: You have lived in local authority care.
Your residential status is 'refugee' or 'humanitarian protection'.
You have participated in the Brookes Engage sustained outreach programmes.
You are eligible for free school meals.
You are under 25 and have caring responsibilities.
You attend a school where average performance is below average at GCSE or in the bottom 40% nationally at A level (or equivalent). Listed as part of a combination with an area criterion.

You live in an area of low participation in higher education, or in an area of higher socio-economic disadvantage. Listed as part of a combination with the school criterion; the page does not name the measure used.

contextual.rulesText: UK students applying for an undergraduate degree (excluding foundation years and foundation degrees) may be eligible for a contextual offer if ONE of these applies: lived in local authority care; refugee or humanitarian protection status; took part in the Brookes Engage sustained outreach programmes; eligible for free school meals; under 25 with caring responsibilities. You may also be eligible if you meet a combination of: attending a school where average performance is below average at GCSE or in the bottom 40% nationally at A level (or equivalent), AND living in an area of low participation in higher education OR living in an area of higher socio-economic disadvantage (the page does not say exactly how these three are grouped). There is no separate form: apply through UCAS and indicate your residential status or care history if relevant.

source.evidence: Our contextual offer is a grade reduction of up to 3 grades below the standard entry requirements.

programmes.name: Brookes Engage
programmes.summary: Free national outreach programme for Year 12 students with masterclass days, online content, student mentoring and a summer school (including an Oxford Brookes Business School Experience stream); completing it gives access to a contextual (lower) offer at Brookes.
programmes.whoCanApply: Students in the first year of a two-year Level 3 course (e.g. A levels or BTEC) at a non-selective state school or college in England, who live in England and are 16 or over, and who also meet at least one widening-participation criterion (for example free school meals or sixth form bursary, care experience, young carer, refugee or asylum seeker, minority ethnic background, or an area in IMD deciles 1-4).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must meet ALL of: first year of a two-year Level 3 qualification; non-selective state school or college in England; live in England; aged 16 or over when starting. AND at least one of: currently eligible for free school meals or 6th form bursary; currently live in local authority care or have lived in care; young carer (under 18); of black or minority ethnic origin; official refugee status or asylum seeker; live in an area of higher socio-economic disadvantage (Index of Multiple Deprivation decile 1-4). Applications are also considered from students with a disability, mental health condition or specific learning difficulty; of minority ethnic origin; with a parent/carer who has served in the armed forces in the past six years; irreconcilably estranged from both birth parents; or from a traveller family.
benefits: Free: travel and meals for in-person activities are provided at no cost
Access to a contextual offer at Oxford Brookes on reduced tariff points, usually around two grades lower (varies per course)
On-campus masterclass days, online content, mentoring from current Brookes students and a summer school (option to stay in halls)
UCAS personal statement support and a special invite to the Open Day and Applicant Days
programmes.offerReduction: Usually around two grades lower than the standard offer, but can vary per course
programmes.subjects: Subject streams include the Oxford Brookes Business School Experience (Accounting and Finance, Business and Management); other streams include Law, Crime and Justice, Architecture, Urban Design and Planning, and Creative Industries

runs.text: Masterclass days from January (Saturday 16 and 30 January), Explore Oxford on Monday 15 February, online guidance on Saturday 20 March; Business School Experience summer school Tuesday 29 June to Thursday 1 July; Year 13 UCAS support from September; mini graduation Saturday 25 March 2028

opens.text: Not stated (the page has an 'Apply Now' link to the application form)

source.evidence: Successful completion of the programme will give you access to a contextual offer to study at Oxford Brookes.

notConfirmed: Application opening date and deadline are not shown on the page

programmes.name: Subject Taster Days 2027
programmes.summary: Free on-campus taster days for first-year sixth form and college students, including an Economics, Accounting and Finance day and a Business, Marketing and Management day.
programmes.whoCanApply: Students at UK schools or colleges in the first year (or repeating the first year) of a two-year Level 3 qualification (e.g. A Levels, BTEC or equivalent). You can apply as an individual or, if you are a teacher or adviser, for a school or college group.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Open to first-year Level 3 students. A travel bursary is paid to students who are eligible for free school meals or a 6th form bursary, live or have lived in local authority care, are young carers, are of black or minority ethnic origin, have refugee or asylum seeker status, or live in an area of higher socio-economic disadvantage (IMD decile 1-4).
benefits: Lectures and interactive academic sessions, practical work, a campus tour and talks on career potential
Travel bursary for students who meet the widening-participation criteria
programmes.subjects: Economics, Accounting and Finance; Business, Marketing and Management; plus other subject areas (e.g. Social Sciences, Law)

runs.text: 2027 dates not announced yet (the page says they will be announced in September)

No 2028-entry pages yet (checked 2026-10-21), so all courses use 2027 entry; the course pages list September 2027 among their start dates.
Oxford Brookes is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of the course pages mention an admissions test.
Every course here also has a 'with Foundation Year' version listed in Brookes' fee finder (https://www.brookes.ac.uk/study/fees).
Brookes' contextual offers are up to 3 grades below the standard requirements and are shown on each course page (for example 104 points instead of 128 for Economics).

Brookes also runs online Year 12 taster sessions (including Business) and recorded subject lectures on its Outreach Hub (https://www.brookes.ac.uk/outreach/post-16); the cost of the taster sessions is not stated on the page.
